title: A turn that starts before its predecessor's closing sighting is recorded closes with assumed_missing_baseline, which voids a clean check's evaluation
outcome: A turn whose source never changed doesn't report an assumed source change just because it started within the few seconds its predecessor's closing report takes, so a clean registered check can be evaluated without any spacing between turns, and a real edit is still reported.
acceptance: A deterministic test, with no timing assumption, shows the defect on the unchanged product: turn A closes with its closing worker gated, turn B starts, A's sighting is then recorded, B closes on unchanged content, and B reports assumed_missing_baseline.
After the fix that same sequence reports no source change from B, including when B closes before A's sighting is recorded.
Negative controls hold: a real edit made during B, before or after A's measurement, is still reported; a refused or undelivered A sighting, a rebind and a root change never supply a baseline.

A pinned real-Engram test on Windows and Linux: a placed clean registered check in turn A, turn B starting before A's sighting is recorded and requesting the evaluator, evaluator records its verdict and done succeeds. No wait is added to a turn or a send.
